source.title: Over-Parameterization Exponentially Slows Down Gradient Descent for Learning a Single Neuron

record.file_problem: The full paper is present and readable; some mathematical symbols are corrupted in the extracted text, but the relevant statements are legible.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies gradient-descent convergence in a new setting: a two-layer ReLU student learning one teacher neuron under Gaussian inputs and population square loss. Its results do not test the benchmark classification conditions named by the versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's own convergence theorems are recorded. The n=1 linear-rate comparison is cited prior work, not this study's result; the figure's plotted values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study establishes convergence rates for learning a single ReLU teacher neuron. It does not test any specified version: in particular, slower convergence does not establish more frequent convergence to spurious minima under V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately captures the authors' conclusion that over-parameterization can change exponential convergence into polynomial convergence. Preserve the distinction that the formal upper bound is for GD and the lower bound is for gradient flow; these are not matching bounds proved for discrete GD. The exponential n = 1 theoretical rate is attributed to prior work, with an empirical comparison in Figure 1.
record.recipe_differences: Synthetic teacher-student learning with Gaussian inputs and population square loss; analyzes convergence rates rather than benchmark classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: The convergence-rate result distinguishes exact parameterization n = 1 from over-parameterization n ≥ 2; within the over-parameterized lower-bound analysis, non-degenerate initialization is required.

fits_no_version.finding: For a single ReLU teacher under Gaussian inputs, sufficiently small random initialization gives over-parameterized GD an O(T^-3) population-loss upper bound. Non-degenerate gradient flow has a matching-order lower bound; special aligned or identical initializations can converge exponentially.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Over-parameterization can slow convergence when learning a single ReLU neuron, despite convergence to a global minimum.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Conference Computational Learning Theory (venue stated in supplied metadata)
record.problems: The results concern a stylized population square-loss problem, not finite benchmark classification; the n = 1 rate comparison is attributed to cited prior work. The lower bound is for gradient flow, and the bounds use asymptotic notation and constants.
record.rows_left_out: The paper mentions Figure 1's empirical loss curves and log-rate trend, but the supplied text provides no recoverable numerical values; those figure-only values were not extracted.

untested.parts: Convolutional networks, CIFAR training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and the stated training recipes.
Spurious-minimum frequency as teacher and student widths grow together, and its reduction with one or two extra student neurons at the specified teacher widths.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization and normalization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation across depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Stability thresholds, loss recovery above them, curvature dynamics, and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to the specified versions, not because the convergence theorems are unreadable. Figure 1's empirical comparison is already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR classification, convolutional networks, corrupted or random labels, model size, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
The study uses a one-neuron teacher and random initialization, but does not measure spurious-minimum frequency or compare students with one or two extra neurons across teacher widths.
Plain versus residual networks, depth, shortcuts, normalization, and the cited special-initialization settings.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, initialization effects on speed or depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian weights.
Learning rates above a stability limit, curvature or sharpness, and divergence thresholds.
Batch normalization comparisons, training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU student network
rows.size_stated: n neurons; n ≥ 2; input dimension d
rows.operation_detail: Randomly initialized gradient descent on population square loss to learn a one-neuron teacher.

conditions.value: wi(0) ∼ N(0, σ²I); σ = O(n⁻⁴²²⁶ d⁻¹ᐟ² ∥v∥)

rows.value: With probability at least 1 − δ, for any T ∈ N, L(w(T + T2)) ≤ O(n⁴∥v∥²/(ηT)³); T2 = O(log n/(nη)).
rows.uncertainty: Probability at least 1 − δ; asymptotic O bound.
rows.note: The theorem states global convergence to a global minimum under its stated synthetic setting; it does not measure training classification error.
rows.check: The result is valid but measures population square-loss convergence, outside all versions. Correct the learning-rate condition to η = O(σ²d/(n^169∥v∥²)); the record omits d and places n^169 in the numerator. Theorem 9 is on printed page 11.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU student network
rows.operation_detail: Randomly initialized gradient flow on population square loss with non-degenerate initialization.
rows.value: L(w(t))⁻¹ᐟ³ ≤ O(n¹⁷ᐟ³(t − T2)/(κ²max(0)∥v∥²ᐟ³)) + γ, where γ does not depend on t.
rows.uncertainty: With probability at least 1 − δ; asymptotic O bound; γ is a time-independent constant.
rows.note: This lower bound on loss decay implies a slow rate in the stated setting; it is a gradient-flow result, not a classification-error measurement.
rows.check: The gradient-flow lower bound is correctly represented but measures convergence speed, outside all versions. It does not demonstrate trapping in spurious minima.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
